As an exercise in topology and learning about this part of mathlib, I'm trying to prove S3≅SU(2)S^3 \cong SU(2)S3≅SU(2).

here's my attempt at the statement:

import Mathlib.Topology.Category.TopCat.Sphere

open Matrix
open TopCat

def S3_homeo_SU2 : sphere 3 ≅ TopCat.of (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) where
  hom := sorry
  inv := sorry

is this the idiomatic way to state this?

And then I would like to follow this mathematical idea:

The natural homeomorphism of R4\R^4R4 onto R4\mathcal{R}^4R4 carries S3S^3S3 onto a subspace of R4\mathcal{R}^4R4 homeomorphic to S3S^3S3 . Since this homeomorphism also preserves the norm of any vector in R4\R^4R4 , the image consists precisely of the unit quaternions and the group of unit quaternions in R4\mathcal{R}^4R4 is SU(2)SU(2)SU(2).

where R4\mathcal{R}^4R4 is the matrix

(ab−b‾a‾)\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ -\overline b & \overline a \end{pmatrix}(a−b​ba​) with (a,b)∈C2(a, b) \in \mathbb{C}^2(a,b)∈C2.

On paper i can probably just write this and call it a day, but I'm not sure how to proceed in lean. Do I just build a chain of equivs going through these steps? any advice appreciated.

(I'm deliberately not using AI for assistance so the questions may be trivial but I don't want AI to one shot this for me)
(also does mathlib want these kinds of result? or maybe this is already in mathlib in some very generalised form, please let me know if that's the case and I can study how it's implemented)
Is the use of category theory intentional?
No, I only saw TopCat.sphere and took me a while to figure out how to use it. Seems like I should be using Metric.sphere instead? missed that somehow thanks
Yeah I think Metric.sphere is the usual way to go
Then you use docs#Homeomorph to state the equivalence

def S3_homeo_SU2 : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 ≃ₜ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) where
  toFun  := sorry
  invFun  := sorry
  continuous_toFun := sorry
  continuous_invFun := sorry
  left_inv := sorry
  right_inv := sorry

yea this makes a lot more sense to me, thanks

Yep. Also, to translate your pen-and-paper proof, you probably don't want to define toFun invFun etc directly here. There should be some lemma that help you to restrict homeomorphism to subspaces, or to transform it in other ways
Something like docs#Homeomorph.subtype
I wuld guess that you do want to just build the maps here?

something like this? The arithmetic and bookkeeping is really quite annoying though...

code

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

open Matrix
open Metric
open Complex ComplexConjugate

def vec_to_mat (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ :=
    !![v 0 + v 1 * I, v 2 + v 3 * I; - v 2 + v 3 * I, v 0 - v 1 * I]

lemma det_eq_norm (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) : det (vec_to_mat v) = ‖v‖ ^ 2 := by
  simp [det_fin_two, vec_to_mat, norm, Finset.sum]
  ring_nf
  norm_cast
  rw [← Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.sq_sqrt]
  simp
  ring
  · positivity

lemma vec_to_mat_unitary_scaled (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) :
    conjTranspose (vec_to_mat v) * vec_to_mat v = ‖v‖ ^ 2 • 1 := by
  ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  · simp [vec_to_mat, mul_apply, norm, Finset.sum]
    ring_nf
    try
      norm_cast
      rw [← Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.sq_sqrt]
      simp
      ring
      · positivity

lemma vec_to_mat_mem_SU2_iff_dist_eq_one (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) :
    vec_to_mat v ∈ specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ ↔ dist v 0 = 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h1
    have normv : ‖v‖ ^ 2 = (1 : ℂ) := by
      rw [← det_eq_norm]; exact h1.2
    norm_cast at normv
    have hv : ‖v‖ = 1 ∨ ‖v‖ = -1 := (sq_eq_one_iff).mp normv
    cases hv with
    | inl h => rw [dist_eq_norm]; simp [h]
    | inr h => linarith [norm_nonneg v]
  · intro h2
    rw [mem_specialUnitaryGroup_iff]
    rw [dist_eq_norm, sub_zero] at h2
    simp [mem_unitaryGroup_iff', star, vec_to_mat_unitary_scaled, h2, det_eq_norm]

def mat_to_vec (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) :=
    !₂[(M 0 0).re, (M 0 0).im, (M 0 1).re, (M 0 1).im]

def S3_homeo_SU2 : sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 ≃ₜ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) where
  toFun := fun x => ⟨vec_to_mat x.1 , (vec_to_mat_mem_SU2_iff_dist_eq_one x.1).mpr x.2⟩
  invFun := fun M => ⟨mat_to_vec M.1, by sorry⟩
  continuous_toFun := sorry
  continuous_invFun := sorry
  left_inv := sorry
  right_inv := sorry

I guess I can brute force my way through this, but I'll be curious to know what's the proper way to prove this and similar results. Maybe from the general result S2n−1≅SU(n)/SU(n−1)S^{2n-1} \cong SU(n)/SU(n - 1)S2n−1≅SU(n)/SU(n−1)? (does mathlib want these kinds of results?)

Is it generally advisable to keep the Equivs separated like above, or fine to integrated like the following once I'm sure I don't need the intermediate steps?

noncomputable def E4RangeHomeomorph : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) ≃ₜ quaternionToR4LinearMap.range :=
    linearIsometryEquivTuple.toHomeomorph.symm.trans
    ((LinearEquiv.ofLeftInverse R4ToQuaternion_leftInverse).toContinuousLinearEquiv
    (F := quaternionToR4LinearMap.range)).toHomeomorph
(I have to say building the equivs is very fun and satisfying, makes me understand the relations between different structures much better)
also is it fine to mark these as simp or generally better to have a separate apply lemma?

ZhiKai Pong said:

also is it fine to mark these as simp or generally better to have a separate apply lemma?

@[simps], it'll generate a separate apply lemma for you. It might ask you to add an exclamation point at the end (@[simps!])

As for separating stuff, it depends on whether you want to have the separate results or not. This style of progressively stronger equivs is common when stronger equivs require stronger hypotheses (e.g. docs#Matrix.comp vs docs#Matrix.compAddEquiv vs docs#Matrix.compRingEquiv vs docs#Matrix.compLinearEquiv vs docs#Matrix.compAlgEquiv)
Many thanks! so if I keep them separate I'll just tag each of them with @[simps!]?
(Also why is this better than a simple @[simp]?)

import Mathlib
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

open Matrix
open Metric
open Complex ComplexConjugate
open Quaternion

def R4 : Submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) where
  carrier := {M | ∃ a b : ℂ, M = !![a, b; -conj b, conj a]}
  add_mem' := by
    intro A B ha hb
    rcases ha with ⟨a1, b1, hA⟩
    rcases hb with ⟨a2, b2, hB⟩
    refine ⟨a1 + a2, b1 + b2, ?_⟩
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [hA, hB]; ring
  zero_mem' := by
    refine ⟨0, 0, ?_⟩
    simp
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  smul_mem' := by
    intro r A ha
    rcases ha with ⟨a, b, hA⟩
    refine ⟨r * a, r * b, ?_⟩
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [hA]

@[simps]
def R4_quaternion_basis :
    QuaternionAlgebra.Basis (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) (-1 : ℝ) (0) (-1) where
  i := !![I, 0; 0, -I]
  j := !![0, 1; -1, 0]
  k := !![0, I; I, 0]
  i_mul_i := by
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  j_mul_j := by
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  i_mul_j := by
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp
  j_mul_i := by
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp

@[simps!]
noncomputable def quaternionToMatrixAlgHom : ℍ[ℝ] →ₐ[ℝ] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ :=
    QuaternionAlgebra.lift R4_quaternion_basis

@[simps!]
noncomputable def quaternionToMatrixLinearMap : ℍ[ℝ] →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ :=
    quaternionToMatrixAlgHom.toLinearMap

lemma quaternionToMatrix_mem_R4 (q : ℍ[ℝ]) : quaternionToMatrixLinearMap q ∈ R4 := by
  simp [R4]
  use q.re + q.imI * I, q.imJ + q.imK * I
  simp [QuaternionAlgebra.Basis.lift, algebraMap_eq_diagonal]
  ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [add_comm]

@[simps!]
noncomputable def quaternionToR4LinearMap : ℍ[ℝ] →ₗ[ℝ] R4 :=
    quaternionToMatrixLinearMap.codRestrict R4 quaternionToMatrix_mem_R4

@[simps!]
def R4ToQuaternionLinearMap : R4 →ₗ[ℝ] ℍ[ℝ] where
  toFun M := ⟨(M.val 0 0).re, (M.val 0 0).im, (M.val 0 1).re, (M.val 0 1).im⟩
  map_add' := by intro A B; rfl
  map_smul' := by intro r A; simp; rfl

lemma R4ToQuaternion_leftInverse :
    Function.LeftInverse R4ToQuaternionLinearMap quaternionToR4LinearMap := by
  simp [Function.LeftInverse, QuaternionAlgebra.Basis.lift,
    algebraMap_eq_diagonal] --works if previous two defs are @[simp] instead

Apologies that I can't come up with a shorter mwe. for the final lemma, tagging the penultimate defs with @[simp] closes the goal, but @[simps!] doesn't. May I ask what's happening here and how should I decide on tagging them?

The issue seems to be that for your last def, simps creates 4 lemmas, one for each output component, and does not create a lemma for the entire output at once. So simp cannot simplify R4ToQuaternionLinearMap x, but it can simplify (R4ToQuaternionLinearMap x).re.

I don't know much about the details of simp/simps and what the correct solution is, but I'd recommend tagging the last def with @[simps apply]. This makes it create the full lemma instead of the 4 parts (see #check R4ToQuaternionLinearMap_apply after adding it).
Perhaps someone more knowledgable than me about this can explain what's going on and what's the best solution.

full proof

import Mathlib
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

open Matrix
open Metric
open Complex
open Quaternion

@[simps]
def quaternionToMatrixLinearMap : Quaternion ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ where
  toFun q :=
    !![(q.re + q.imI * I), (q.imJ + q.imK * I);
      -(q.imJ - q.imK * I), (q.re - q.imI * I)]
  map_add' := by
    intro q1 q2
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp <;> ring
  map_smul' := by
    intro r q
    ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp <;> ring

noncomputable def R4 : Submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) :=
    quaternionToMatrixLinearMap.range

@[simps apply]
def matrixToQuaternionLinearMap : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ →ₗ[ℝ] ℍ[ℝ] where
  toFun M := ⟨(M 0 0).re, (M 0 0).im, (M 0 1).re, (M 0 1).im⟩
  map_add' := by intro A B; rfl
  map_smul' := by intro r A; simp; rfl

lemma quternionToMatrix_leftInverse :
    Function.LeftInverse matrixToQuaternionLinearMap quaternionToMatrixLinearMap := by
  simp [Function.LeftInverse]

noncomputable def quaternionToR4LinearEquiv : Quaternion ℝ ≃ₗ[ℝ] R4 :=
    LinearEquiv.ofLeftInverse quternionToMatrix_leftInverse

noncomputable def quaternionToR4CLE : ℍ[ℝ] ≃L[ℝ] R4 :=
    quaternionToR4LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv

noncomputable def quaternionToR4Homeomorph : ℍ[ℝ] ≃ₜ R4 :=
    quaternionToR4CLE.toHomeomorph

@[simps!]
noncomputable def E4RangeHomeomorph : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) ≃ₜ R4 :=
    linearIsometryEquivTuple.toHomeomorph.symm.trans quaternionToR4Homeomorph

lemma E4RangeHomeomorph_det (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) :
    det ((E4RangeHomeomorph x).val) = ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by
  simp [norm, Finset.sum]
  ring_nf
  norm_cast
  rw [← Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.sq_sqrt]
  simp
  ring
  · positivity

lemma sphere_det_equiv (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) :
    dist x 0 = 1 ↔ det ((E4RangeHomeomorph x).val) = 1 := by
  rw [E4RangeHomeomorph_det]
  norm_cast
  simp
  intro
  linarith [norm_nonneg x]

noncomputable def sphereRangeHomeomorph :
    {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4) | dist x 0 = 1} ≃ₜ {M : R4 | det (M.val) = 1} :=
    E4RangeHomeomorph.subtype sphere_det_equiv

lemma quaternionToMatrix_det_eq_norm_sq (q : Quaternion ℝ) :
    det (quaternionToMatrixLinearMap q) = normSq q := by
  simp [normSq_def']
  ring_nf
  simp
  ring_nf

lemma R4_det_one_mem_unitary (M : R4) (h : det M.val = 1) :
    M.val ∈ specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ := by
  rw [mem_specialUnitaryGroup_iff]
  refine ⟨?_, h⟩
  rcases M.property with ⟨q, hM⟩
  rw [mem_unitaryGroup_iff]
  ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp [mul_apply, ← hM]
  · ring_nf
    simp
    trans (normSq (R := ℝ) q)
    · rw [normSq_def']; norm_cast; ring
    rw [← h, ← quaternionToMatrix_det_eq_norm_sq, hM]
  · ring
  · ring
  · ring_nf
    simp
    trans (normSq (R := ℝ) q)
    · rw [normSq_def']; norm_cast; ring
    rw [← h, ← quaternionToMatrix_det_eq_norm_sq, hM]

lemma SU2_mem_R4 (M : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) : M.val ∈ R4 := by
  simp [R4]
  use ⟨(M.val 0 0).re, (M.val 0 0).im, (M.val 0 1).re, (M.val 0 1).im⟩
  simp
  have ⟨hu, hdet⟩ := mem_specialUnitaryGroup_iff.mp M.property
  have hMM := mem_unitaryGroup_iff.mp hu
  have Minvstar:= inv_eq_right_inv hMM
  have Minvadj := inv_def M.val
  simp [hdet] at Minvadj
  symm at Minvstar
  rw [star_eq_iff_star_eq, Minvadj, adjugate_fin_two] at Minvstar
  rw [← Minvstar]
  have eq11 := congrArg (fun A => A 1 1) Minvstar
  have eq10 := congrArg (fun A => A 1 0) Minvstar
  simp at eq11 eq10
  ext i j; fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
  simp
  · rw [eq10]; simp [add_comm]
  · rw [eq11]

def R4DetHomeomorphSU2 : {M : R4 // det M.val = 1} ≃ₜ specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ where
  toFun := fun M =>
    ⟨M.val, R4_det_one_mem_unitary M.val M.property⟩
  invFun := fun SU =>
    ⟨⟨SU.val, SU2_mem_R4 SU⟩, (mem_specialUnitaryGroup_iff.mp SU.property).2⟩
  left_inv := by simp [Function.LeftInverse]
  right_inv := by simp [Function.RightInverse, Function.LeftInverse]
  continuous_toFun := by fun_prop
  continuous_invFun := by fun_prop

noncomputable def S3_homeo_SU2 :
    sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 4)) 1 ≃ₜ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :=
    sphereRangeHomeomorph.trans R4DetHomeomorphSU2
